title: Regional makerspace access list
background: A fictional network wants one access identity per member, while allowing shared household contact details and distinct memberships at different sites. Membership numbers are issued locally by each site.
observations: An ordered policy accepts an equal member number first, sends conflicting verified birth years to review second, accepts equal email third, and otherwise leaves entries separate. The first applicable row wins.
A proposed declarative table evaluates all rows together and selects the highest numeric action code. Its author has not specified whether action codes represent priority or severity.
Regression fixtures were created by replaying decisions from the ordered policy. The only manual observations are a few lockout complaints. Some sites omit birth year and households may share email.
Staff want to simplify policy maintenance and describe a passing regression suite as evidence that the new table improves member accuracy.
constraints: Unauthorized access from a false association is more harmful than an extra manual badge check.
The planning team may propose synthetic witnesses and a human review study, but cannot change access decisions or obtain private member records.
request: Write a refactoring decision note that compares an implementable low-complexity option with the table proposal and specifies how to assess behavioral change and member-level effects.
